source: Questionnaire for Non functional requirements, Sridharrajdevelopment, Medium, 10 December 2023 (questions verbatim); mapped to ISO/IEC 25010:2023

questions.text: What will be the application load time/pre-load time for clients/users?
questions.help: Code can show page-performance measurement; load times themselves need a measurement or your target.

questions.text: What is the access pattern — number of users, concurrent access?
questions.help: User numbers are your input; the code can show connection pools, caching and rate limits.

questions.text: How can we handle the network latency for each action or interaction made to the applications?
questions.help: Caching and performance defects (database work in loops, costly operations) come from the code; latency targets come from you.

questions.text: What would be the projected growth in consumption/transactions?
questions.help: Growth is your input; the code can show unbounded queries that will not cope with it.

questions.text: How can we secure the applications/data from unauthorised access?
questions.help: Authentication libraries, hard-coded secrets and missing access checks come from the code; your identity provider and roles from you.

questions.text: How can we protect the applications/data from malicious attacks?
questions.help: Injection, weak cryptography, unsafe HTML and vulnerable dependencies come from the code checks.

questions.text: How can we adhere to the local laws, regulations and auditing standards?
questions.help: Your team names the regulations and signs off; refactorX collects evidence and never certifies compliance.

questions.text: How can we recover the application from an outage?
questions.help: Retries and messaging libraries come from the code; your recovery plan from you.

questions.text: How can we minimise the recovery time from the time the event of an outage is identified?
questions.help: Health endpoints and an automated build pipeline come from the upload; the recovery time objective (RTO) from you.

questions.text: How can we recover the lost data?
questions.help: Versioned database migrations come from the code; backups and the recovery point objective (RPO) from you.

questions.text: What would be the impact in terms of costs, between the time the disaster happens and the system if recovered?
questions.help: Only your team can answer this.

questions.text: How can we ensure the application is continuously monitored and automated alerts are in place?
questions.help: Metrics, tracing and logging libraries and alert rules kept in the upload; alert routing from you.

questions.text: What about the application support in case manual remediation is required?
questions.help: Runbooks in the upload and maintainability problems (architecture smells, rule breaches, hard-to-read code).

questions.text: How can we make sure the application performs consistently?
questions.help: Automated tests, retry and circuit-breaker libraries, and defects that cause inconsistent behaviour.

questions.text: How can we inspect and correct glitches?
questions.help: Tracing, structured logging and error-tracking libraries.

questions.text: How can we ensure the high/continued availability of an application?
questions.help: Health endpoints and job locking across instances come from the code; deployment checks come later; the availability target from you.

questions.text: How can we make an application fault tolerant?
questions.help: Circuit breakers, fallbacks and messaging; hub-like parts are potential single points of failure.

questions.text: How can we meet the increasing demand for any kind of resources?
questions.help: Caching and asynchronous processing; database work in loops limits scale.

questions.text: How can we achieve a good scale for a sudden spike in utilisation demand?
questions.help: Queues and rate limiting come from the code; autoscaling checks come later; peak load from you.

questions.text: How can we simplify an application’s use?
questions.help: Little comes from code (internationalisation); usability testing is your input.

questions.text: How can we achieve a seamless user experience?
questions.help: Accessibility checks kept in the upload; your accessibility target (for example WCAG 2.2 AA).

questions.text: What operating systems the applications might have to get deployed/supported?
questions.help: Container definitions and pinned runtime versions come from the upload; supported platforms from you.

questions.text: How should data exchange happen between different kinds of application tires/layers?
questions.help: API descriptions (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI) and messaging libraries.
